What are all the gun laws and restrictions in the United States?

It depends on where you are. Some places you can walk around with your gun on your hip or carry a rifle with no permit (open carry). Some places you can't have a weapon on you without a permit. Some places have no conceal carry at all. Some places are gun free zones some welcome CC permit holders. Some places don't let you have 30 round magazines some do. It's a large country with many different laws from state to state.
Depends on the city and state. The areas with the highest gun violence have the highest restrictions. The nigger cities for example.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun_law_in_the_United_States

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun_laws_in_the_United_States_by_state

There's hardly any at the federal level (biggest one is probably full-auto requires special permit), but every state has its own restrictions. Local governments can also restrict further.

Usually, without a permit you can buy a gun and keep it at home (your yard and car are included in this). You can also carry it around when doing some applicable activity like hunting or target practice. You can carry it while directly on your way to the activity or your home/car also. Typically long guns (rifles and shotguns) can also be carried without a permit (you may need to put an orange cap on the muzzle) but some idiots might freak out and call the cops on you anyway.

Red states (most of them) let you get a carry permit which lets you carry a handgun wherever. Those usually distinguish open carry from concealed (whether people can see your gun). Some places allow only open, some only concealed, there's no real logic to it. It's a dumb distinction IMO, probably made up during some knee-jerk public reaction. There are a few states that allow you to carry without a permit as well.

Purple states like Colorado are similar, except for major cities which resemble blue state in their laws. Practically every major US city is overwhelmingly liberal.

Blue states tend to restrict as much as they can get away with. Bans on long guns, hand guns, black guns (yes there are literally laws about guns looking too scary/black), magazine sizes, where you store ammo, where you store guns, you name it. I think they all allow carry permits in theory, because banning them outright would be too hard to defend in court (it's unconstitutional after all) but in practice they just stall your application and bury you in paperwork so it's very hard to get one.

However regardless of all this, anybody can decide they don't want you to carry on their property. If they tell you not to, and you don't immediately leave, that's criminal trespass with a firearm, and can get you into a lot of trouble. So in major cities of states that do not restrict, you'll see a lot of stores and establishments that ban guns. So you end up with a situation where you can carry all you want, but it's not practical because you can only walk up and down the street and can't actually go into any business.
